title: Laws of thermodynamics
summary: In 1824 the French engineer Sadi Carnot, studying how steam engines work, showed that an engine produces work by moving heat from a hot body to a cold one, so no engine can be fully efficient. His book was little noticed until the 1850s, when Rudolf Clausius and William Thomson (later Lord Kelvin) joined his insight to the conservation of energy, giving the First and Second Laws of thermodynamics. Clausius named entropy in 1865, and the new science spread across Europe.

uncertainty.note: Carnot published Réflexions in 1824; Clausius introduced the term entropy in 1865.
